reranked_evidence.title: Police attack Cockroach activists as thousands march on Indian parliament - Al Jazeera
reranked_evidence.snippet: *More than 10,000 protesters braved tear gas and baton charges in their largest challenge yet to PM Modi’s government.*. Police have fired tear gas and attacked supporters of the youth-led Cockroach movement with canes and baton charges as more than 10,000 marched towards India’s parliament in New Delhi in the largest protest yet demanding the resignation of the education minister and a crackdown on corruption in the exam system. The march on Monday by the protesters who ironically call themselves the Cockroach Janta Party to mock the name of the ruling party of Prime Minister Narendra Modi was even bigger than expected, with numbers swelled by anger at Saturday’s forcible hospitalisation of veteran 59-year-old activist Sonam Wangchuk, who has been on hunger strike for three weeks in solidarity with the movement. Modi’s government, shaken by the emergence of the Cockroach movement in May, offered a minor concession by inviting two activists to meet a senior cabinet minister for talks.

reranked_evidence.title: India’s Cockroach protests: Rahul Gandhi detained after calling for PM Modi to resign - The Guardian
reranked_evidence.snippet: Opposition leader taken away after accusing Narendra Modi of ‘destroying the future of India’s youth’ during protest in solidarity with cockroach movement. Indian police briefly detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday during protests calling for prime minister Narendra Modi’s resignation, in solidarity with the new youth-led cockroach party movement. Gandhi, the leader of India’s Congress party, staged a sit-in outside Modi’s house on Tuesday afternoon, stating that Modi must resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth”. His protest took place as thousands of students were gathered at a separate site in central Delhi, the day after a huge protest calling for the resignation of Modi’s education minister was met with brutality by Delhi police, including baton attacks and teargas. Gandhi said his party was taking their protest directly to the prime minister’s house, after the Modi government refused to take up the issues of the students and the alleged “brutality unleashed on students” in parliament.

reranked_evidence.title: How India's youth-led 'Cockroach' movement challenges Modi - DW.com
reranked_evidence.snippet: # How India's youth-led 'Cockroach' movement challenges Modi. What started as a satirical protest against exam leaks in India has grown into a wider movement voicing young Indians' anger over jobs and education. Riot police fired tear gas and used batons in New Delhi as tens of thousands of supporters of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) marched towards India's Parliament on Monday (July 20). The CJP began as an online campaign in May and rapidly evolved into a Gen Z street movement, giving a voice to a generation frustrated by unemployment, shrinking opportunities and a failing education system. The youth-led "Cockroach" party is now posing an unexpected challenge for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, prompting a response that combines political outreach with police action. This is a worthless government," Renuka Chowdhury, an MP from India's opposition Congress party, told DW. The CJP movement gained fresh momentum over the weekend after veteran reform activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose three-week hunger strike has become a symbol of the protests, was forcibly taken to a hospital by police.
